title: רב דימי <small>סתם הוא</small> בר יוסף

paragraphs: Rav Dimi without qualification is bar Yosef, not bar Rav Yosef, for Rav Dimi preceded him. Perhaps he is a brother of Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef; a student of Rabbi Yochanan. When Rav Dimi came, he reported Rabbi Yochanan. Abaye said to him, “Did Rabbi Yochanan say this?” He called Rav Dimi “karkefana”; Rashi explains: an important man. To me it appears to be an expression for “head,” like karkafeta in the tefillin expression, and likewise Rabbi Yishmael’s karkafalo. The Arukh explains: one with a skull. As for Yuchasin’s statement that Abaye called Rav Dimi karkefana, the reason is that Eruvin 22 says: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, “In the Land of Israel one incurs no liability on account of a public domain.” Rav Dimi was sitting and reporting this teaching. Abaye said to Rav Dimi, “What is the reason? If you say …; perhaps you mean ascents and descents?” He answered, “Karkefana, I saw your head among the pillars when Rabbi Yochanan said this teaching.” Likewise in Yevamot 78, end of side a: “Karkefana, I saw your head among the pillars when Rabbi Yochanan said ….” Tosafot writes in both places: Rav Dimi said to Abaye, “Karkefana”—a great man—“I saw your head,” meaning Rabbah, who was Abaye’s teacher. Rabbah went up to the Land of Israel (see his entry) to study before Rabbi Yochanan, but we have not found that Abaye went to study Torah there. (Moreover, Abaye did not see Rabbi Yochanan; R.Sh.L.) His teacher Rabbah, however, was Rabbi Yochanan’s student and was in the study house at the time Rabbi Yochanan said this teaching. End of quotation. Thus Rav Dimi called Abaye karkefana. Understand this. Rav Dimi said to Abaye, “By God, my own eyes saw, and not another’s; I heard it from Rav Yirmeyah’s mouth; Rabbi Yirmeyah from Rabbi Zeira; Rabbi Zeira from Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi; Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi from Rav”: chapter Chavit, 145a. Rav Dimi was sitting and reporting, and Abaye raised an objection: Nazir 36a. In chapter Tefillat HaShachar, when he and Rav Avya were in Rav Yosef’s study house (see his entry, for an error slipped in before him). When Rav Dimi came, he said, “Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehudah Glustera said” (see his entry). When he went up to Nehardea, he sent word: “The things I said before you were mistaken in my hands; rather, it is thus …”: Shabbat 63b. In Shabbat 136: the son of Rav Dimi bar Yosef was mourning an infant who died within thirty days, whose months of gestation had been completed. In Asheri: the daughter of Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak. Agra was his father-in-law (see his entry). He reported Rabbi Elazar: beginning of Sukkah chapter 2; chapter Chezkat HaBatim, 53b; chapter Mi Shemet, 150a. He reported Rabbi Ammi, who reported Rabbi Chanina: Keritot 25b. Rabbi Ammi, Rabbi Assi, and Rav Bibi: Shabbat 74a. When Rav Dimi came, he said: Zeiri said in the name of Rabbi Chanina, Shabbat 50a. Rav Chiyya may be his brother. He reported Rabbi Chama bar Yosef; he reported Rabbi Chanina, Shabbat 125b. Rav Yosef (see above). When Rav Dimi came, he reported Rabbi Yochanan: Eruvin 87b, 101b. He reported Rabbi Yonatan; he reported Rabbi Yannai, there, 75a; Menachot 26b. Rav Dimi said: Rabbi Yitzchak ben Avdimi said in Rabbi’s name. When Rav Dimi went up, he found Rabbi Yirmeyah sending to Rav Yosef. Merimar in Rav Dimi’s name. Rav Mesharshya, son of Rav Dimi. He reported Rav Nachman: Bava Batra 121a. He asked Rav Nachman: Chullin 12a. He came for judgment before Rav Nachman concerning his sister. This is not so: the wording of the Gemara, Bava Batra 151b, is that Rav Dimi’s sister came before Rav Nachman to seek judgment against her brother Rav Dimi. Rav Nachman sent him word: if he does not come, place him under a ban; see there. When he came, he said: Rav Nachman bar Kohen expounded. He reported Rav; he reported Rabbi, Zevachim 118b. He came from the Land of Israel before Ravin: Rashi, Chullin 106a. Rav Rechumi sat before him. Yishmuel [ישמואל, as printed] said to him, “Go and examine this woman”: Ketubbot 60, side a. Shmuel said to him, “Go and frighten that woman”: Niddah 66a. From this it appears that he was Shmuel’s student. The Ari writes that Chizkiyah was reincarnated in Rav Dimi. This is the secret of bedmi, an expression of Rabbi Dimi: “I am deprived of the rest of my years.” The years that Chizkiyah would not live were lived afterwards by Rav Dimi, for reincarnated persons complete their missing years and deeds (G.N.).
